transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what made me come in is that... the things that usually make me feel like myself have just started feeling really flat and heavy lately. 

I'm usually a pretty engaged guy. I go on photography walks, I mentor some kids, and I'm an executive assistant, so even just keeping a really clean, organized calendar is something I normally take pride in. But recently, I've just stopped initiating any of it. It just feels like too much effort, and I'm not getting anything out of those things anymore. So, I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone about it.
How long have you been feeling this way—when did you first notice this loss of interest and heaviness starting?

I'd say it's been going on for about a year and three months now. 

It really started after a family member of mine had some changes in their health and behavior. I ended up having to step in and take on a lot more of the coordination to help manage things for them. And, yeah, that's right around when I first noticed this heavy feeling starting to set in.
Over these past 15 months, has this heavy, flat feeling been present pretty much every day without a break, or have there been stretches—even a few weeks—where you felt back to your normal self?

Well, it hasn't been just the heavy feeling the whole time. There have been breaks, but... not really where I felt like my normal self, either. 

There are these stretches where I actually feel unusually upbeat, like everything is just clicking perfectly. I'll feel really good. But then, during those times, even a tiny change—like if someone at work just moves a meeting on the calendar—can make me really sharp with people. I snap at them in a way that honestly surprises me. So, it's not always flat, but the upbeat times don't feel quite right either.
When you have one of these upbeat, everything-clicking stretches, how long does it typically last—just a day or two, or several days in a row?

Well, they definitely last more than a day or two. Usually, it's several days in a row, sometimes a week or more. 

Honestly, for most of this whole fifteen-month period, I've been cycling back into those stretches. I get really driven, feeling like I can handle anything, and I end up taking on way too much. I sleep a lot less during those times, too. There are some quieter weeks here and there, but mostly it's been this back-and-forth between the heavy feeling and these overconfident, high-energy periods.

During the 'heavy' periods you described, have you ever had a stretch of at least two weeks where, along with feeling low, you also noticed things like changes in your sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, or feelings of worthlessness or hopelessness?

Well, I guess... I'm not really sure if it's been exactly two weeks at a time, or if all those things happen together. I mean, the heavy feeling is there, but I don't know if I've really paid attention to my appetite or concentration during those specific times. It just feels low, you know? I haven't really tracked it like that.
Looking back over these 15 months, has there ever been a stretch of two months or more where you felt completely normal—no heaviness and no upbeat, overdriven periods?

I'm honestly not sure. I mean... it's hard to look back over the whole fifteen months and measure it out exactly like that. But two whole months? I don't think so. 

There might have been a couple of quiet weeks here and there where things settled down, but a full two months without the heavy feeling or those overdriven stretches? I really haven't noticed a gap that long where I just felt completely normal.
During those upbeat, high-energy stretches, do you also notice things like your thoughts racing, feeling unusually confident or important, or being easily distracted?

Yeah, I definitely get that unusual confidence. When I'm in one of those stretches, I'll start feeling like I'm the only one who can actually straighten things out. Like, I'll look at the doctors, my family, the way the office is running, and I just... I start believing that my system is better than anyone else's judgment. I get really convinced that I know exactly how everything should be handled.
During those heavy, low periods, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight?

Not really, no. My weight stays pretty much the same. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I haven't really paid close attention to my appetite, but... I mean, I'm still eating. I haven't noticed any big swings in my weight or anything like that when things get heavy.
During those upbeat, high-energy stretches, do people close to you—family, friends, coworkers—notice a clear change in how you're acting compared to your usual self?

I don't really know for sure. I haven't really asked anyone if they notice a difference. I mean, they might see me working faster or taking on more stuff, but nobody has actually come up to me and said I'm acting totally out of character or anything like that. So... I can't really say if it's a clear change to them.

During those high-energy, overconfident stretches, has your work, finances, or relationships ever been seriously disrupted or harmed—for example, getting in trouble at work, overspending, or a big conflict with someone—because of how you were acting?

No, I wouldn't say anything like that has happened. I mean, I might get a little pushy about how things should be organized at work, but it hasn't led to any real trouble. I haven't blown through my savings or gotten into any big blowouts with my family or anything. It's more just... I feel like I have all the answers, but it hasn't actually ruined anything in my life.
